transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in. Can you tell me what’s been bringing you here today?

I guess… things at work have gotten strange. Since I got that county safety award, some people have been twisting my inspection reports, asking these budget questions like they’re trying to make me look dishonest. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but it doesn’t feel that way. It feels coordinated, like they’re trying to discredit me.
Can you tell me more about how you know these changes to your reports and budget questions are part of a coordinated effort against you?

It’s hard to explain without sounding… I don’t know. But it started after that safety award. Reports that were fine before suddenly came back with wording changed, or questions attached that made it look like I was hiding something.

And the budget questions aren’t normal questions. They’re pointed. Like they’re trying to catch me saying something wrong. My supervisor says it’s just review, but it doesn’t feel random to me. It feels like certain people are trying to make me look crooked.
Have you felt like people have been trying to harm or deceive you in any other areas of your life, not just at work?

Not really outside of work, no. It’s mostly been there… since the safety award. The reports getting changed, the budget questions—they feel aimed at making me look dishonest. My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but I don’t buy that. It feels coordinated.
Do you ever feel like people are trying to harm or trick you in situations outside of work, like at home, in public, or with friends?

No… not really at home or with friends. It’s mainly work. Since that county safety award, certain people there have been changing my reports and asking those budget questions like they’re trying to make me look crooked. My supervisor keeps saying it’s normal review, but… I can tell it’s coordinated.
Do you have any thoughts about why these changes and questions are happening at work, even if others might not see it the same way?

I think it’s because of that county safety award. After that, it’s like certain people didn’t like the attention I got or something.

I know my supervisor says it’s just normal review, but the way my reports get changed and the budget questions come up… it feels pointed. Like they’re trying to make me look dishonest. I can’t prove every piece of it, but I can tell it’s coordinated.
Do you believe that these changes to your reports and the budget questions are happening because someone is deliberately targeting you, even if there’s no clear evidence to support that?

Yeah… I do. I mean, I know there isn’t some document proving it or anything, but since that county safety award, it’s been different.

The report changes, the budget questions… they don’t feel random. It feels like certain people are trying to make me look dishonest, like they’re coordinating it to discredit me. My supervisor calls it normal review, but I don’t really believe that.
Do you think any of your coworkers share your concern about these changes to your reports and the budget questions, or is this something you’ve noticed that others don’t seem to pick up on?

I don’t think most of them say it out loud, no. Some probably notice, but they act like it’s just normal paperwork stuff.

It’s more something I’ve picked up on because it’s my reports getting twisted, and those budget questions are aimed at me. Since that award, it just feels… coordinated. Like they’re trying to make me look crooked.
Have you ever had any experiences outside of work where you felt like people were plotting against you or trying to harm you in some way?

No… not really outside of work.

It’s mainly been there, since that safety award. The reports getting changed, the budget questions… it feels like they’re trying to make me look crooked. Outside of that, I don’t really have anything like that to point to.

When you say people are trying to make you look dishonest by changing your reports and asking these budget questions, do you feel like this is something that could be proven with evidence, or do you feel certain about it even without being able to show it to someone else?

I mean… I think it could be shown if someone really looked at the report changes and the questions they keep asking.

But even without some smoking-gun proof, I feel pretty certain. Since that county safety award, it’s been too specific. The reports get twisted, then the budget stuff comes up like they’re hinting I did something wrong. My supervisor says it’s normal review, but… it doesn’t feel normal to me. It feels coordinated.
Have you ever experienced any thoughts or beliefs that might seem strange or hard to believe to others, like thoughts that involve things that couldn't possibly be true?

I wouldn’t say it’s impossible or anything like that.

It’s just… at work, since that county safety award, certain people have been changing how my inspection reports read and asking these budget questions in a way that makes me look dishonest. My supervisor says it’s normal review, but I can tell it’s more coordinated than that.
Have you ever had any thoughts or beliefs that others might find unusual or hard to believe, even if they weren’t related to work?

Not really. I mean… nothing outside of work comes to mind.

It’s mostly this thing with my inspection reports and the budget questions after the safety award. That’s what people might not believe, I guess, but to me it’s pretty clear what they’re doing.
Have you ever had any thoughts or beliefs that others might not understand or that you couldn’t explain in a way that made sense to them, even when you tried?

Yeah… I guess this work thing is like that.

I’ve tried explaining it, but people act like I’m reading too much into it. Since that county safety award, the way my inspection reports get changed, and then the budget questions they ask… it feels pointed. Like they’re trying to make me look crooked.

My supervisor says it’s just normal review, but… I don’t know. I can tell it’s coordinated, even if I can’t make everyone see it.
Have you ever had any beliefs or ideas that you know others would find hard to believe, even when there’s no proof to support them?

I mean… I don’t have paperwork proving it, if that’s what you mean.

But yeah, people probably wouldn’t believe me about work. Since that county safety award, certain people have been changing my inspection reports and asking budget questions in a way that makes me look dishonest. My supervisor keeps saying it’s just normal review, but… I can tell it’s coordinated. Like they’re trying to discredit me.

Even though your supervisor has told you that the changes to your reports and the budget questions are just part of the normal review process, do you still feel certain that people are deliberately trying to discredit you, even if you can’t fully explain why?

Yeah. I mean… I know what my supervisor says, but I don’t buy that it’s just routine.

Ever since that safety award, the report changes and those budget questions feel too pointed. Like they’re trying to make me look crooked. I can’t lay it all out perfectly, but… yeah, I’m pretty sure it’s coordinated.
Have you ever had any beliefs or experiences that you know sound impossible or hard to prove, even to people who know you well?

Yeah… I guess so.

I know it sounds hard to prove. But this thing at work—after the county safety award—my reports started getting twisted, and then the budget questions came up in a way that made me look bad. My supervisor says it’s normal review, but… I don’t think it is.

It feels coordinated. Like someone’s trying to discredit me.
